\textbf{Source.} Tadelis (2013), \emph{Game Theory: An Introduction}, Exercise 7.1 ``Strategies'', p.~147 {[}PDF 166{]}. Reproduced verbatim. Answer in the source: none in the book (the preface, p.~xiii, says about half are solved on Princeton UP's website; not checked).

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Strategies:} Imagine an extensive-form game in which player \(i\) has \(K\) information sets.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  If the player has an identical number of \(m\) possible actions in each information set, how many pure strategies does he have?
\item
  If the player has \(m_k\) actions in information set \(k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, K\}\), how many pure strategies does the player have?
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
